title: Chatstream Event
description: One item of a chat stream (go-chatstream Event). The struct is flat: the fields of every verb sit side by side, and which are meaningful depends on verb. On the wire the SSE id field carries the cursor (the hub's seq); the JSON seq is 0 until the client copies the id into it.

v.description: Schema version; "1". The schema is additive-only: a consumer ignores what it does not know.

seq.description: The hub's cursor for this event. Decoders leave it 0; the SSE id carries it on the wire.

run_id.description: The run this event belongs to.

time.description: When the decoder produced the event (RFC 3339).

verb.description: What the event means. A Verb, or a verb a newer producer added; consumers ignore verbs they do not know.

parent_run_id.description: run.start: the run this one continues.

reason.description: run.finish: a FinishReason. run.abort: the cause. approval.request: why. gap: a gap reason.

raw_reason.description: run.finish: the dialect's own word for the finish reason.

code.description: run.error: the error code (see ErrorCode; a dialect's own codes pass through).

retryable.description: run.error: whether a retry may succeed.

kind.description: part.start: a PartKind. activity: the namespaced activity kind ("nanite.slot_changed").

meta.description: part.start: conventions such as name, call_id, is_error, detail, phase, url, media_type, title, filename, source_id.

text.description: part.delta: appended text (text, reasoning, refusal parts).

final.description: part.end: a tool_call's parsed arguments, a reasoning part's signature or encrypted value.

call_id.description: approval.request: the tool_call part the approval is for.

descriptor.description: approval.request: an opaque description of what is being approved.

Verb.description: What an Event means. The scope nesting is run > step* > message > part*. run.finish, run.error and run.abort are terminal.

FinishReason.description: Why a run finished, in one closed vocabulary. "cancelled" is spelled as ACP and AG-UI spell it.

ApprovalMode.description: How an approval is answered: on the same connection (inband), or by ending the run and starting the next one (suspend).

UsageScope.description: What a usage report covers: cumulative (a later report replaces an earlier one), final (the run's totals, once), or delta (reports add up).

GapReason.description: Why events were lost. Generated by the hub or its framing layer, never by a decoder.

ErrorCode.description: Run error codes a decoder or hub synthesizes. A dialect's own codes pass through run.error code and are not limited to these.

Usage.description: Token usage as DISJOINT components: no token is counted in more than one field, so the total is a plain sum and cannot double-count.

uncached_input.description: Prompt tokens that were neither read from nor written to a cache.

cache_read.description: Prompt tokens served from a cache.

cache_write.description: Prompt tokens written to a cache.

output.description: Generated tokens other than reasoning tokens.

reasoning.description: Generated reasoning tokens, when reported separately; otherwise they are inside output.

extra.description: Provider counters that are not tokens of the run's own text. Never part of the total.

total.description: Derived by the Go encoder (the sum of the five components); ignored on decode. Never trust it over the components.

Raw.description: An upstream event preserved as received.

payload.description: The upstream payload; a JSON string when the bytes were not JSON.
